units.summary: Defines passage-time and time-constant setup, establishes the norm/shape framework and states foundational limit-shape results used by later FPP arguments.
Read the stated argument and model discussion through p.45; the subsection continues onto p.46, which was not read, so no complete-subsection claim is made.
Surveys large-deviation and fluctuation estimates, separating assumptions for upper/lower tails and recording the limits of existing bounds.
Introduces the geodesic framework and uniqueness/direction questions used in planar FPP.
Develops directional geodesic and coalescence results, with differentiability/uniqueness hypotheses tracked separately from conjectural behavior.
Introduces Busemann limits, their existence mechanisms and uses for infinite geodesics and directional structure.
Treats Eden/Richardson growth and competing growth, including the growth rule and its relation to passage-time models.
Sets up max-flow/min-cut formulations and the principal flow asymptotics discussed in the survey.
Checked the survey’s open-question statements relevant to archived FPP, geodesic and growth problems.
Read for source tracing and to distinguish cited theorems from the survey’s own discussion.
Defines the stationary edge-FPP environment, rays and Busemann differences; records the good-measure hypotheses and shape input.
Defines two-type Richardson growth from competing sources and states the positive-probability coexistence conclusion.
Reduces coexistence to ruling out ray-independent Busemann differences, then to a finite-energy local edge modification.
Uses monotone ray limits, symmetry/additivity, ergodic averaging and a shape lower bound for contradiction; finite energy and conditional absolute continuity create two competing infections.
Read the cited shape, ergodic and growth-model sources to preserve the proof’s dependency trail.
States the two-point-weight FPP variance theorem and its Talagrand influence strategy, then introduces a product-graph auxiliary estimate.
Combines symmetry, edge influences and the discrete product-space inequality to bound the circumference variance on a finite vertex-transitive graph times a cycle.
Randomly shifts endpoints to spread pivotal-edge influence, sums influences along a bounded-length geodesic, and obtains the logarithmic variance denominator.
Proves the discrete entropy/influence inequality used in the main argument; the auxiliary randomized endpoint bits are included in the variance accounting.
Read the cited inequality and earlier FPP variance results to identify which inputs are imported.
Defines directed exponential vertex-LPP and sets out direction, multiplicity and coexistence questions.
States the dense countable exceptional-direction theorem, uniqueness for each fixed direction, and positive-probability finite-source coexistence.

units.unit: §3 Local modification of the geodesic tree
units.summary: Conditions on diagonal last-passage data and uses the continuous exponential density to force a prescribed finite tree shape with positive probability.
Uses planar order, competition-interface atomlessness and the local-modification lemma to establish directional multiplicity and coexistence claims.
Read to identify the exact Ferrari–Pimentel and Coupier–Heinrich inputs.
Identifies the average-distance convergence problem, the geodesicity criterion, and the paper’s equivalence between the two rates.
Sets FPP and concentration assumptions, states the quantitative shape and average-metric results, defines strong asymptotic geodesicity, and introduces the invariant-metric equivalence.
Uses Talagrand concentration over all vertex pairs in polynomial-volume balls; a union bound and Borel–Cantelli yield eventual uniform approximation by the average metric.

units.unit: §3 Strong asymptotic geodesicity of the average metric
units.summary: Transfers a random-metric geodesic to the average metric on a good environment, controlling the geodesic’s location by the positive linear lower bound and exponential edge tails.
Completes the strong-asymptotic-geodesicity estimate with the rate N(r)=c√(r/log r), using the concentration approximation and a subdivision point along a random geodesic.

units.unit: §5 Strong asymptotic geodesicity implies a limit-shape theorem
units.summary: Subdivides long metric segments and convexifies the resulting displacement vectors to obtain a Hausdorff rate for the invariant norm ball.

units.unit: §6 Limit shape implies strong asymptotic geodesicity
units.summary: Uses norm-ball convergence and finite direction nets to construct approximate metric subdivisions in the reverse direction.
Shows that the subcritical zero-weight condition forces a positive linear lower bound on expected passage distance.
Read for the imported concentration, shape theorem and asymptotic-geodesicity inputs.
States critical square-lattice edge-FPP mean, variance and limit-law results and outlines the invasion-percolation/circuit strategy.
Sets near-critical quantiles and correlation lengths, and assembles planar RSW, circuit and invasion-cluster estimates.
Builds crossings between successive near-critical circuits using separated attachment points and conditional tail bounds.
Transfers annular passage estimates to the inverse-quantile series and closes the logarithmic-radius mean asymptotic.

units.unit: §5 Universality of limiting variance and limit laws
units.summary: Decomposes centered passage times into circuit-indexed martingale increments, compares to Bernoulli increments, and invokes mixing plus a dependent-array CLT.
Read the percolation, invasion and dependent-CLT sources on which the planar proof depends.
Introduces exponential edge-FPP and the high-dimensional construction of a short slab-crossing path.
Selects successive low order-statistic edges in disjoint hyperplanes and optimizes the number of stages and quantile levels.
Repeats independent slab crossings and applies the law of large numbers to obtain the stated upper bound on the time constant.
Read for the exact prior Dhar bound and the theorem’s FPP context.

units.unit: §1 Eden model, definitions and previous results
units.summary: Defines the uniform infected-boundary-vertex Eden growth rule and distinguishes it from edge-clock exponential FPP; states the dimension-22 improvement.
Derives a finite-dimensional recursion for expected boundary growth and reduces the theorem to explicit inequalities for its coefficients.
Documents the finite numerical procedure used to certify the displayed d=22 parameter inequalities; this is supporting computation, not a proof for every d≥22.
Gives executable recurrence details and finite numerical outputs supporting the theorem at the claimed dimension.
Read to verify the earlier d=35 result and model conventions.
Introduces general i.i.d. nonnegative vertex-weight directed LPP, its time constant, Busemann increments, the adjacent-covariance problem, and prior KPZ context; no exponential weight law is imposed.

States the local-mgf assumption for general i.i.d. vertex weights, defines pre-Busemann assumptions, and gives the covariance/time-constant equivalence, sufficient rate-function criterion, and Bernoulli application.

units.unit: §3.1 Covariance and the time-constant: Proof of Lemma 2.3
units.summary: Uses the Legendre transform of the concave shape slice, recovery and past independence to derive the adjacent-increment covariance identity and prove its equivalence to comparison with the exponential benchmark shape.

units.unit: §3.2 Coarse graining argument: Proof of Theorem 2.4
units.summary: Truncates large weights using the local mgf, coarse-grains up/right paths into a countable class, and combines path entropy with a Cramér rate gap to bound the time constant.
Proves Proposition 2.5 by conditional Jensen; equality of first and second moments would force equality in law, ruling out the proposed strict convex-order comparison.
Proves the sufficient Bernoulli rate-function criterion and threshold p*≈0.6504 by differentiating the explicit binary rate function and bounding logarithmic terms.

units.unit: Appendix A: Existence of Busemann functions
units.summary: Records shape differentiability/support-line conditions under which directional Busemann limits exist; the main theorem itself is stated for pre-Busemann functions.

units.unit: Appendix B: Busemann correlations and the KPZ relationship
units.summary: Gives a conditional heuristic connecting global increment covariance inequalities to variance and KPZ exponents; the hypotheses and exponent identity are not proved here.
Read acknowledgments and bibliography for source attribution, especially the pre-Busemann, convex-duality, coarse-graining, and KPZ inputs.

sources.reading_scope: Entire arXiv v2 PDF, physical pages 1–22 read; section names and page ranges verified against the original contents/headings.

units.summary: Defines the rescaled domain network, source/sink boundary patches, max flow and continuum cut value; states the surface-order LLN and positivity criterion.
Defines cylinder costs and directional surface tension, invokes finite max-flow/min-cut, and constructs the anisotropic continuum perimeter/min-cut functional.
Surveys prior straight- and tilted-cylinder max-flow LLNs, including moment assumptions and attribution to earlier authors.

Presents existing surface-order lower- and volume-order upper-deviation theorems as companion-paper results [7] and [8], then explains their Borel–Cantelli role; physical p.14 remains within this subsection.

Theorem 11 approximates each finite-perimeter separator by a transverse polyhedral separator while controlling symmetric-difference volume and anisotropic perimeter; the proof uses reduced-boundary differentiation, Vitali covers, local cylinder comparisons, and boundary-collar perturbations to establish equality of continuum cut values.
Under a finite first moment, proves positivity iff Λ(0)<1−pc(d), using positive directional surface tension and geometric lower bounds for every separating surface.
Read the references to identify which cylinder-flow deviation estimates are imported from the two companion papers, distinct from this paper’s polyhedral approximation theorem.
Frames planar edge-FPP bigeodesic questions and identifies direction sectors and shape differentiability as central.
Defines two alternative assumption packages, including the precise second-moment condition E[(min of four incident weights)^2]<∞ in A1′.
States sector-directed existence, convergence/coalescence and no-bigeodesic results, plus endpoint-independent sector Busemann limits under differentiability assumptions.
Explains the relation of the geometric argument to the ferromagnetic model, without using it to weaken the stated FPP hypotheses.
States the planar BKS midpoint result and explains its bigeodesic contradiction mechanism.
Reviews prior directed/undirected geodesic tools and the ordering framework used in the planar argument.
Outlines extremal sector rays, half-plane limits and the passage from left/right equality to Busemann limits.
Establishes directional trapping, the measurable full-probability event X, and upper-half-plane subsequential-geodesic controls; propositions and corollaries provide the half-plane limits used later.
Defines the total order on full-plane and half-plane sector geodesics modulo coalescence and proves the order properties used to construct extremal paths.
Uses the order and leftmost/rightmost intersections on horizontal lines to construct extremal sector geodesics and show their directional/geodesic properties.
Uses planar ordering, uniqueness and finite-energy modifications in the Burton–Keane argument to force coalescence.

units.unit: §5 Equality of left- and rightmost geodesics
units.summary: Combines planar crossing/Busemann inequalities with differentiability to identify equal slopes and eliminate distinct extremal rays.
Uses coalescence, mass transport and the no-backward-branch argument to conclude the sector no-bigeodesic theorem.
Read the full list to trace imported uniqueness, finite-energy and planar-ordering results.
States triangular-lattice critical vertex-FPP mean and variance limits and sketches the Bernoulli comparison and annular-circuit construction.
Sets up critical Bernoulli coupling, nested circuits, arm events and the moment notation used by both limit theorems.
Uses good closed circuits and separated attachment points with conditional Chernoff estimates to build a path with asymptotically negligible excess cost.
Compares the constructed path with the Bernoulli geodesic and sends the near-critical slack to zero to identify the logarithmic mean constant.
Compares annular martingale increments with Bernoulli increments, bounds their discrepancy by arm/circuit estimates and imports the exact variance limit.
Read to trace Yao’s Bernoulli limits and the triangular-lattice RSW, arm and CLT inputs.
States expectation approximation, Gaussian lower-tail concentration and separate outer/inner shape-rate conclusions with their moment assumptions.
States the low-moment Gaussian lower-tail bound, introduces entropy and pivotal-edge estimates, and derives concentration by the Herbst method.
Establishes tensorization and block localization identities for the entropy of passage time under product edge weights.
Bounds entropy by resampling/pivotal-edge counts and controls the exceptional long-path contribution using the small-time tail.
Applies the Herbst entropy method to derive the Gaussian lower-tail concentration inequality.
Combines the expected-distance approximation and lower-tail estimate with endpoint union bounds and Borel–Cantelli.
Combines logarithmic-box concentration with low-moment upper-tail estimates; the stronger moment condition and distinct logarithmic power are retained.
Read the full bibliography for Alexander, Kesten, Zhang and Ahlberg estimate provenance.

Derives the graphical Hammersley dynamics, Rule 1/Rule 2, and the scaling and space-time interchange properties.
States Theorem 5 (c=2 and the local Poisson limit) and gives a PDE heuristic; the article explicitly says the heuristic is not the proof.
Constructs the full-line process, classifies finite-intensity translation-invariant stationary laws as mixtures of Poisson laws, and proves space-time interchange.
Couples the empty-half-line process to a stationary rate-b full-line process and optimizes E L(x,t)≤bx+t/b at b=√(t/x).
Develops monotone couplings, local expectation increments and the derivative limit that yields tight diagonal local distributions and identifies mean intensity.

Takes diagonal subsequential local limits, uses stationarity/translation invariance and Poisson-mixture classification, applies space-time interchange and the rate inequality for c≥2, and identifies the unit-rate local limit.
Surveys known LIS concentration/deviation results and separates proved one-sided statements from anticipated asymptotics.
Read the complete bibliography and source trail; the local manuscript references occupy pp.17–18.

units.summary: Defines the uniform-permutation LIS, states the Tracy–Widom and moment theorems, and reduces the fixed-size problem to a Poissonized Toeplitz determinant and Riemann–Hilbert analysis.
Sets the orthogonal-polynomial RHP and the Painlevé-II model problem used to construct the local critical parametrix.

units.unit: §3 Toda lattice and Painlevé III connection
units.summary: Derives the differential/difference identities relating the Toeplitz determinant and its recurrence coefficients to the Toda/Painlevé-III structure.
Solves the logarithmic-energy equilibrium problem and identifies the phase transition at the critical ratio 2√λ/(k+1)=1.
Transforms the RHP with the g-function and estimates orthogonal-polynomial coefficients away from the critical point.
Constructs the outer and local parametrices across the support transition and obtains uniform coefficient asymptotics.

units.unit: §7 Asymptotics of the Poissonized distribution φ_n(λ)
units.summary: Sums logarithms of the orthogonal-polynomial leading coefficients to get the Poissonized distribution and tail estimates.
Proves the transfer inequalities that recover fixed-N LIS probabilities from the Poissonized distribution.
Combines the double-scaling asymptotics, de-Poissonization, and tail integrability to prove distributional and moment convergence.

units.unit: Appendix A: Poissonized Toeplitz determinant identity and heuristic
units.summary: Supplies an alternate derivation of Gessel’s determinant formula and a heuristic for the leading √N scale; this is not the theorem proof.
Read the bibliography and source trail for Robinson–Schensted, Toeplitz determinants, Riemann–Hilbert steepest descent, and Tracy–Widom.

Defines undirected edge FPP and the three cylinder passage times; states admissibility, the finite-moment width threshold, and fixed-width results; reviews exponent conjectures and separates directed vertex-LPP comparisons.
Defines Z×G_n passage/crossing times and states the graph-width CLT under diameter/edge-count growth assumptions.
Uses subadditivity and connector bounds to compare endpoint, cylinder, and side-to-side passage times and identify the limiting mean speed.
Applies Doob decomposition, resampling one edge, and a pivotal-edge lower bound to obtain variance at least order n/k_n.
Controls fluctuations by pivotal-edge counts, Efron–Stein-type moment inequalities, and Kesten’s exponential estimate for long cheap paths.
Reduces to side-to-side crossings, approximates them by independent blocks with diameter-cost connectors, applies Lyapunov/Rosenthal, and recursively reblocks to close the exponent gap.
Proves positive linear mean/variance limits and a Brownian functional limit for a fixed finite graph cross-section.

units.unit: §8 CLT up to a height threshold
units.summary: States unproved fluctuation, transversal, curvature, and variance-monotonicity assumptions and derives the conditional threshold theorem.

units.unit: §9 Proof of the conditional height-threshold result
units.summary: Bounds boundary mismatch by shape/transversal estimates, inductively controls cylinder variances and moments, and applies a two-type blocking Lyapunov argument.
Reports Bernoulli-weight simulations and regression/QQ plots for conjectured variance and CLT behavior; these are finite computational evidence.
Read the acknowledgments identifying simulation and presentation contributions.
Read all cited concentration, shape, critical-FPP, LPP, and probability sources to record proof dependencies.

Disintegrates limiting laws to the original environment and derives directional, all-direction, graph-coalescence, and associated geodesic coalescence conclusions.
Proves the measurability needed to integrate/disintegrate the family of limiting Busemann measures.
Read the cited FPP shape, Busemann, finite-energy, ergodic, and planar-geodesic sources.
Read the article identity, abstract, assumptions announced for the corner-growth model, and stated contribution.
Explains the Busemann/cocycle program, variational motivation, and the shape-regularity and percolation-cone regimes.

Develops convex duality between the point-to-line and point-to-point shape functions and parameterizes dual tilts across nondifferentiable segments.
Constructs stationary recovery cocycles, defines stationary LPP, proves monotonicity/continuity, and identifies cocycle minimizers of the variational formulas.
Proves cocycle bounds on liminf/limsup endpoint increments and obtains true Busemann limits when shape differentiability collapses the bounds.

units.unit: §7 Cocycles from queueing fixed points, including §7.1
units.summary: Builds coupled tandem-queue fixed points, verifies Burke-type stationarity and cocycle/recovery identities, and derives explicit exponential/geometric special cases.

units.unit: Appendix A: Ergodic theorem for cocycles
units.summary: States the cocycle ergodic theorem imported in the sublinearity/shape comparison arguments.
Read the complete bibliography for queueing, shape, variational, cocycle, and integrable LPP dependencies.
Read source identity, abstract, model interpretations, and the promised GUE Tracy–Widom fluctuation statement.
Defines geometric vertex corner growth, its random-Young-diagram/TASEP representation, and exact shape, large-deviation, and fluctuation theorems, including the exponential limit.
Derives the discrete Coulomb-gas representation from tableaux/Young diagrams and proves the large-deviation principle through a variational equilibrium measure.
Expresses the distribution through the Meixner-polynomial kernel and sets up the determinant asymptotics.
Carries out the upper/lower large-deviation estimates by discretized energy bounds, compactness, and equilibrium-measure comparison.
Uses contour/integral representations and double-critical-point asymptotics to obtain Airy-kernel scaling.
Solves the equilibrium variational problem and verifies the measure/support used in the shape and large-deviation arguments.
Read the full reference list for the combinatorial, orthogonal-polynomial, random-matrix, and TASEP inputs.
Introduces planar i.i.d. edge-FPP, the limit shape, and the questions about non-polygonality and fluctuations.
Defines the class of laws with a minimum-weight atom at or above the oriented-percolation threshold and identifies the flat-edge endpoints.
States endpoint differentiability, growth/coexistence consequences, and the separate variance/exponent results with their assumptions.

units.unit: §2.1 Differentiability of the limit shape at percolation points
units.summary: States Theorem 2.1 and the accumulation of extreme points; fixes the endpoint and symmetry consequences.
States infinite coexistence and the infinite-ends consequence when the law is not purely atomic; these are FPP infection-time results.
Defines χθ and ξθ, states the logarithmic and n^(1/4) lower bounds and χ–ξ relation, preserving the distinct moment, non-random-fluctuation, and curvature premises.

units.unit: §3.1 Strategy of the proof of Theorem 2.1
units.summary: Assumes a second tangent and derives a positive transverse linear functional whose expected advance will contradict the shape limit.
Embeds oriented percolation in minimum-weight edges and invokes the finite-set survival estimates needed for bypass construction.
Builds positive-probability local configurations and iterates bypasses to gain a linear expected f-coordinate advance.

units.unit: §3.4 Proof of Theorem 2.1, case p > oriented pc
units.summary: Uses supercritical survival, shape convergence, and the bypass gain to contradict the hypothesized second tangent.

units.unit: §3.5 Proof of Theorem 2.1, case p = oriented pc
units.summary: Sprinkles edges with weights in (1,K] to a supercritical auxiliary parameter, applies the same contradiction, then lowers the parameter to criticality.
Applies Newman–Piza resampling influences, proves geodesics use non-minimal edges outside the cone, localizes them to annuli, and sums over logarithmically many scales.
Uses the influence lower bound, geodesic confinement, and shape geometry to derive the stated χθ–ξθ inequality.
Read the full bibliography to trace oriented-percolation, shape, concentration, and Newman–Piza inputs.
